description:
FILED s474b (Fable, 2026-09-07) -- USER: "Sounds good" to the recommended order (1) #1061, (2) this, (3) widen (#1504).  Ordered by the USER, so blockedBy #1061.

WHY: the 14-dist board (183 files; 78 PASS / 54 PARTIAL / 51 FAIL; 2,140 ok / 342 not ok at s467) is not consumed, and unlike the sweep (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, column 6) and the companion (#1501) it has NO row-level baseline: tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl --tsv writes one line per t-file (dist, file, verdict, ok, notok, rc), so a file can lose a row and gain a row and read unchanged, and no row has a cause.  The s343/s344 cause files (baselines/cpan-board14-fail-causes-s343.tsv 53 rows, -partial-causes-s344.tsv 65 rows) are per FILE, a month stale, and read by nobody.

JOB (the #993 I1 + s473t2 shape, board-flavoured):
 1. tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl gains a row-level output (`--rows FILE`; rule 11: reuse the TAP parsing it already does for the counts): one line per FAILING assertion -- dist, t-file, test number, description, got/expected when the TAP diagnostics carry them, and a CAUSE column.  Blessed as baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv with a header; the board diff (whatever compares two --tsv snapshots today -- check tools/ for it; if it is a hand `diff`, add the comparison to the scoreboard) prints `CAUSES: N of M blessed row(s) have no cause` like tools/sweep-diff.pl.  Descriptions are Test::More's (join keys, docs/tap-assertion-audit.md); an unnamed row is keyed like the sweep keys it (#1041: an empty description stands for all of a file's unnamed rows).
 2. The 342 not-ok rows: cluster by got/expected shape per file, probe ONE representative per cluster with tools/run-dist-t.pl vs real perl on the same file (oracle rule 1: always run real perl beside the board -- perl itself SKIPs author tests and *-report-prereqs.t; rule 2: never -I<dist>/lib for Scalar-List-Utils), attribute (existing task / NS:<section> / new task with the reproducer and the row count).  The known families from s344 are the starting point: Text-Balanced ~300 (#237 family, mostly closed by s378-s467 -- re-measure), Sub-Uplevel/`caller` 127 (#233), Scalar-List-Utils 110 (#238, #1286), Capture-Tiny (#201), role/method-modifier (#135).  A cluster fixable in <= 1 h with no new mechanism SHIPS (own commit, gate, guard, rows leave by edit); the rest are FILED.
 3. The 51 FAIL files (zero ok): each names its first failing line or the perl-side SKIP that makes it a board artifact (s343 counted 12 artifacts of 53) -- a FAIL that is "perl skips it too" gets the cause `PERL-SKIP` in the row file, so the FAIL column stops counting them as PCL failures (or the scoreboard gains a SKIP verdict; say which and why).

BARS: every row in the new file has a cause (CAUSES 0 of N); the per-file snapshot re-taken on the final tree with every moved file explained in its header (never re-blessed over a hand note); real perl run beside it; gate green; corpus-diff IDENTICAL unless a fix shipped (then the fix's own bars); a DECIDED section with the cluster -> task table.

=== DONE (s473w, 2026-09-09) ===

ALL THREE JOB STEPS, plus two instrument bugs the first run found.

STEP 1 â THE INSTRUMENT.
  * `tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl --rows FILE` â one line per FAILING assertion:
    `dist, t-file, num, description, got, expected [, cause]`, the sweep's
    `baselines/fail-baseline.tsv` shape one column wider.  Join key
    (dist, file, DESCRIPTION); an unnamed row keys on the empty description and
    #1041's rule then makes one key stand for all of a file's unnamed rows.
  * A file that produced NO TAP gets a synthetic `*FILE*` row (num 0,
    description `*FILE*`) whose `got` names what happened â
    `no TAP rows (rc=N)` or `1..0 # SKIP <reason> (rc=0)`.  Without it the 50
    FAIL files could not appear in a file of failing assertions and `PERL-SKIP`
    would be unwritable.  38 of the 183 files are in that state.
  * ONE TAP parser, `tools/lib/PCLTap.pm`, feeding both the counts and the rows
    (rule 11).  Its counts are deliberately the HISTORICAL `/^ok \d+/` and
    `/^not ok \d+/`, with a TODO directive recorded on the row and never
    subtracted â a counting change would move every blessed snapshot for a tool
    reason.
  * `--diff BASELINE CURRENT [--board-baseline F --board-current F]` prints
    NEW / FIXED / LOST, `TOTAL passing: baseline N, current M`, and
    `CAUSES: N of M blessed row(s) have no cause`; it says `LOST: NOT CHECKED`
    when the per-file tables are absent, and exits nonzero on NEW or LOST â
    `tools/sweep-diff.pl`'s contract exactly.
  * TIMEOUT ALLOWANCES: `baselines/cpan-board-timeouts.tsv`, read through
    `tools/lib/PCLTimeouts.pm` â the companion runner's inline reader,
    extracted and verified identical against the live
    `baselines/perl-suite-timeouts.tsv` (same keys, same seconds, same cause
    text, `timeout_for` agreeing at defaults 90 and 500).  Effective timeout =
    max(row, --timeout); the allowances in effect are announced per run.
  * GUARD `tools/t/cpan-scoreboard.t`: 25 rows, ~8 s wall, NOT in the Pl/t gate
    (it forks SBCL).  Over a two-file fixture dist it pins the per-file table,
    a named failure with got/expected, an unnamed failure, the `*FILE*` row of
    a self-skipping file, the announced allowance, the SBCL wait-status line
    and all four --diff outputs including "LOST: NOT CHECKED".

TWO INSTRUMENT BUGS THE FIRST RUN FOUND, both fixed here:
  * #1512 fault 1: Text-Balanced 05_extmul.t needs ~150 s against a 120 s
    timeout, so the board recorded `FAIL 0 0 124` and every row was invisible.
    With the registry's first row the file reads PARTIAL 16/14.
  * A SIGNAL-KILLED RUN IS NOT A VERDICT.  `run-dist-t.pl` threw away the SBCL
    child's wait status, so an OOM-killed run published its empty TAP as
    `FAIL 0/0` â measured: two Algorithm-Diff files read FAIL 0/0 in a loaded
    board run and 32/3 + 102/20 alone.  `--rows` now reports the status and the
    scoreboard re-runs such a file SERIALLY, once, taking the serial verdict.

STEP 2 + 3 â THE CENSUS.  Real perl was run beside all 183 files with the same
@INC rule (`scratch/.../oracle.pl`), and every zero-row file's first error was
captured.  Every failing row has a cause; `CAUSES: 0 of N`.  Seven files real
perl SKIPS too and carry `PERL-SKIP` (the scoreboard still calls them FAIL â
changing the verdict would silently rewrite four earlier snapshots, so the
cause column is what stops them counting as PCL's).  The biggest clusters:
#233 caller() fidelity (Sub-Uplevel, 129 rows), #1568 Text::Balanced extract_*
(55), #155 tie + #201/#1509 Capture-Tiny, #135 role composition, the
Scalar-List-Utils introspection bundle #1571, #930 lvalue subs, NS:DynaLoader
for the XS-only modules, NS:Warnings-gated diagnostics (#221).

SHIPPED FROM THE CENSUS: #1525 (`scalar(HASHREF)`) and #1507 (`use overload`
is a BEGIN).  MEASURED AND FILED: #1506 (needs a `lib/constant.pm` shim),
#1512 (profiled).  FILED NEW: #1567, #1568, #1569, #1570, #1571, #1572, #1573,
#1574, #1575, #1576.

BLESSED: `baselines/cpan-board14-fails.tsv` (row level, with the header naming
the command, the perl-side skips and the chdir caveat #1575) and
`baselines/cpan-board14-s473w.tsv` (per file, taken on the final tree).
`baselines/cpan-board14-fail-causes-s343.tsv` and `-partial-causes-s344.tsv`
are marked SUPERSEDED in their own headers (kept â they are history).
